reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the cited text supports it: Section 17(b) (p0118) gives Sparkling (Customer) an unconditional right to terminate 'at any time' on 90 days' written notice, with no cause requirement, which sits at the top of the playbook fallback notice range (60-90 days).
No early-termination fee, penalty or acceleration attaches to the Customer's exit, which is better than the fallback tolerance of a fee up to three months' fees.

No Vendor (Garman) convenience right appears anywhere in the cited termination provisions - Section 17 limits termination to Sparkling's 17(b) right and mutual insolvency/uncured material default - so the walk-away trigger is absent.

The failed deterministic check ('Customer convenience termination present') is a wording artefact: the clause does not use the labels 'for convenience'/'without cause' but requires no trigger, so substance controls.

Correctly handled as internal evidence: no redline (rendered text is identical to the original) and no counterparty comment, and the shortfalls against the preferred position (90 rather than 30 days' notice; no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees) are recorded as observations rather than escalated as deviations.
